commit.message:
Replace simulation test with a VOPR-style deterministic simulator

Add a simulator/ workspace crate modeled on TigerBeetle's VOPR. The seed
drives the whole configuration: replica count, client count, request
rate, idle periods, heartbeat interval, and network loss, replay, and
delay are all drawn from the seed's PRNG. A run has a safety phase with
faults active until every request is replied to, and a liveness phase
with faults disabled in which the cluster must converge.

Properties checked every tick: commit number monotonic, state machine
matches the committed log prefix, committed prefix agreement across
replicas, no duplicate ops, replies match commits, and convergence at
the end.

The seed can be a git commit hash, and CI runs the simulator with the
commit under test so failures reproduce from the commit alone. Panics in
replica code are caught so the seed is always printed.

Replica gains read-only accessors so properties can inspect it. The old
tests/simulation_test.rs is removed; simulator/simulator_tests.rs checks
the simulator itself for determinism and a few fixed configurations.

 ## Testing
 
-You can run the tests with:
+Run the unit tests and the simulator regression tests with:
 
 ```console
-cargo test -- --nocapture
+cargo test --workspace
 ```
 
-The run will print out a *seed* value such as:
+### Simulator
 
-```console
-Seed: 10693013600028533629
-```
+The `simulator/` crate is a deterministic simulator for the library, modeled
+on TigerBeetle's VOPR. It runs a cluster of replicas and a set of clients in a
+single thread, passes messages through a simulated network that can lose,
+replay, and delay them, and checks a set of properties after every tick.
 
-If the simulation triggers a problem, you can reproduce the exact same run by passing a seed to the simulator:
+The seed determines the whole configuration: cluster size, request rate, idle
+periods, and network fault probabilities are all drawn from the seed's PRNG.
+A run has two phases. In the safety phase, faults are active and the clients
+submit a fixed number of requests. In the liveness phase, faults are disabled
+and every replica must converge to the same fully committed log.
+
+Run it with a random seed:
 
 ```console
-SEED=10693013600028533629 cargo test -- --nocapture
+cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator
 ```
 
-You can also increase logging level to see more output of the run with:
+Every run prints its seed. To reproduce a run, pass the seed as an argument:
 
 ```console
-RUST_LOG=debug cargo test
+cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- 10693013600028533629
 ```
 
-You can get a test coverage report with:
+A 40-character git commit hash is also accepted as a seed, which is what CI
+uses, so a CI failure is reproducible from the commit alone:
 
 ```console
-cargo tarpaulin -o html
+cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- $(git rev-parse HEAD)
 ```
 
+Use `--lite` for a small cluster with fewer requests, and see `--help` for
+overrides such as `--requests-max` and `--packet-loss-probability`. Set
+`RUST_LOG=debug` to see every request and message delivery.
+
 ## References
 
 The implementation of `vsr-rs` is based on the paper [Viewstamped Replication Revisited](https://pmg.csail.mit.edu/papers/vr-revisited.pdf) by Liskov and Cowling.

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+[package]
+name = "vsr-simulator"
+version = "0.1.0"
+edition = "2021"
+description = "Deterministic simulator for vsr-rs"
+publish = false
+
+[lib]
+name = "vsr_simulator"
+path = "lib.rs"
+
+[[bin]]
+name = "vsr-simulator"
+path = "main.rs"
+
+[[test]]
+name = "simulator_tests"
+path = "simulator_tests.rs"
+
+[dependencies]
+anyhow = "1"
+clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }
+crossbeam-channel = "0.5"
+env_logger = "0.9.1"
+log = "0.4.17"
+rand = "0.8.5"
+rand_chacha = "0.3.1"
+vsr-rs = { path = ".." }
